## Not for young children

Six Flags recommends Fright Fest for guests 13 and older; families with younger children are directed instead to the daytime Kids Boo Fest, which runs on the same calendar of dates without the haunted-house content.

## Fright Fest — edition 2026

Fright Fest 2026 runs select nights from September 26 through October 31 at Frontier City, with a new Nightmare Mansion maze joining returning haunted attractions, three scare zones and a lineup of live shows, alongside the daytime Kids Boo Fest for younger visitors.

## 2026 season

The 2026 lineup adds a new maze, Nightmare Mansion, alongside returning haunted attractions Cadaver Castle, Forgotten Freaks, Terror of Prosperity and Midnight Mausoleum. Scare zones include Clown Town, Silent Night Slaughterhouse and Doll House. Live entertainment across the season includes The Cremation, Deadman's Party, Escape from Prosperity, DJ Extreme, Freakshow Deluxe, the Festival of Fright Parade, Magic of the Night, Proctor's Revenge and Zambora. The event runs on Frontier City's general fall calendar alongside Food & Brew Festival weekends and the daytime, family-oriented Kids Boo Fest, which shares the same September 26 – October 31 date range without the after-dark scare content.

✔ How the endocrine system uses hormones to control body activity, and how it works alongside the nervous system to maintain homeostasis

# About the Workshop

Image: IOHA Live from the Lab: Skin, Connective Tissues, & Joints 2-Hour Workshop

### Discover the structural reality of the skin, connective tissues, and joints in a single, focused 2-hour in-lab live-stream anatomy workshop.

Using cadaveric specimens broadcast in real time, you'll explore the skin, connective tissues, and joints up close, gaining evidence-based insights that directly apply to your practice, studies, or personal understanding of the human body, from wherever you are.

Unlike our 3-hour anatomy workshop, which provides a broad overview of multiple regions and systems of the body, this workshop focuses specifically on the skin, connective tissues, and joints, offering a deeper cadaver-based learning experience.

This workshop is designed for a broad audience, from movement and bodywork professionals to nursing and pre-med students, health and wellness practitioners, and anyone with a genuine curiosity about the human body, all from wherever you are.
